newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: City of Prague seen deciding intl bond Friday.
newsitem.headline: City of Prague seen deciding intl bond Friday.

text.p: The Prague city council recessed on Thursday before reaching a decision on a proposed $300 million international bond issue, a spokewoman for city hall told Reuters.
"They should get to it tomorrow before noon," Michaela Kynkorova told Reuters.

The city's executive sent a plan to the full city council on Thursday calling for a five to seven year international issue to finance transport infrastructure projects, but the government and central bank have criticised the idea.
No market or currency has been specified for the issue, which Kynkora said was expected to carry a coupon of around seven percent with an expected launch date in September or October.

Government and central bank officials have warned the city against going ahead with the issue because it would bring a large amount of new funds into circulation at a time when the economy is struggling to keep the money supply in check.

The Czech economy was shaken in late May by a speculative attack on the crown which forced the central bank to float the currency and it fell to more than 15 percent below its highs against the dollar and mark in early February.

The controlled float of the currency was backed by a rise in key interest rates and a government austerity package meant to slow domestic demand and dampen the inflationary effects of the crown's depreciation.
Prague carries an indicative investment-grade "A" rating from Standard & Poor's, the same as the Czech sovereign debt.
Kynkorova said that an arranger for the issue would be chosen by a public tender.
